objects.original: An objective f and its actual gradient-descent map T_h=id-h∇f.
objects.reconstructed: A C² real-valued objective and its actual Riesz gradient map on E.
objects.evidence: Riesz identification on Euclidean space agrees with the ordinary gradient. The full module derives H from fderiv of fderiv f and derives DT; no arbitrary oracle replaces the objective.

domains.original: The exercise is on all of R^d, under the Section 3 C² convention.
domains.reconstructed: All complete real inner-product spaces, including infinite-dimensional and zero spaces.
domains.evidence: Euclidean spaces instantiate the Lean domain. The Riesz/symmetric-Rayleigh/Bochner segment argument supports the wider domain, which is a genuine generalization, not literal equality of source and Lean domains.

quantifiers.original: Global curvature assumptions; any two points x,y; a uniform bound for the gradient step; balanced choice minimizing that bound.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For every compatible objective, parameters and x,y, the balanced bound and a scalar comparison for every real h.
quantifiers.evidence: The endpoint declaration covers only hessian-segment-bound, as explicitly bound in candidate metadata; the optimal declaration supplies balanced-minimax-step. No pairwise/local-to-global quantifier swap occurs. The comparison being inside ∀x,y is harmless on an inhabited vector space.

assumptions.original: C² globally; α-convexity and β-smoothness. Definitions 1.5 and 1.12 use nonnegative moduli; the κ contraction interpretation is the positive regime 0<α≤β.
assumptions.reconstructed: Global C², StrongConvexOn α, actual-gradient quadratic upper model, 0≤α≤β and β>0.
assumptions.evidence: Source smoothness is exactly the one-sided quadratic upper model, not a separately assumed norm Lipschitz gradient. C² is explicitly Section 3 convention, not a proof convenience. Signed moduli (endpoint) and α=0 (optimal) enlarge the regime; existing assumption ledger/lesson discloses them. A minimizer, used elsewhere in the notes, is unnecessary for a two-point update estimate.

conclusion.original: Derivative endpoint bound followed by the balanced step and the condition-number two-point factor.
conclusion.reconstructed: Two-point bound with q=(β-α)/(α+β), and q≤max(|1-hα|,|1-hβ|) for every real h.
conclusion.evidence: The component binding prevents claiming the endpoint lemma alone solves minimization. For α>0, substituting κ=β/α gives exactly q=(κ-1)/(κ+1). The second declaration minimizes the endpoint envelope, not the actual Lipschitz constant of an individual objective.

scopes.original: A deterministic Euclidean norm/operator-norm estimate via the actual Hessian and segment FTC.
scopes.reconstructed: A deterministic global norm estimate using symmetric continuous linear maps, Rayleigh supremum, and an actual continuous segment derivative.
scopes.evidence: Read the entire supplied module and lesson: Hessian lower/upper forms are derived; symmetry follows from C²; h≥0 gives the Rayleigh interval; continuity supplies interval integrability; FTC and the norm estimate finish the bound. The zero-vector Rayleigh convention is explicitly explained. No statistical, almost-everywhere, iteration-complexity or minimizer-existence conclusion is smuggled in.

constant_dependencies.original: Step 2/(α+β), factor (κ-1)/(κ+1), κ=β/α, uniform in points/objective.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: Step 2/(α+β), q=(β-α)/(α+β), depending only on α,β.
constant_dependencies.evidence: The source specialization has α+β>0. The optimal proof balances the endpoints and adds β M≥β(1-hα) and α M≥α(hβ-1), giving (α+β)M≥β-α. It retains α=β and explicitly labels α=0 as nonexpansive; no dimension or hidden regularity constants occur.

deltas.description: Intentional Hilbert-space generalization; full statements are not literally domain-equivalent.
deltas.evidence: Candidate assumptions and lesson identify the domain expansion; restricting to E=R^d gives the source proof component.

deltas.description: Intentional α=0 nonexpansive extension beyond the κ>finite positive-curvature interpretation.
deltas.evidence: The extension is stated in the declaration/lesson and does not replace the source regime. Neither extension is proposed as a source repair.

deltas.description: Scalar envelope comparison includes every real h.
deltas.evidence: The weighted endpoint proof works for negative h too. The chosen balanced h is positive; no actual-gradient bound for every negative step is claimed here.
